videos.title: Every WW2 Rifle RANKED — WORST to BEST
videos.description:
Every WW2 Rifle RANKED — from the worst clunker ever shoved into a soldier's hands to the one gun that quietly ended an entire era of warfare.

By 1945, most soldiers on Earth were still fighting with a bolt-action design older than their grandfathers — yank the bolt by hand between every single shot. But buried in that same war was a weapon so far ahead of everyone else that soldiers are still carrying its grandchildren into battle today.

In this video we rank the 15 most iconic rifles of World War 2 — WORST to BEST. From Germany's embarrassing Gewehr 41 failure, to the legendary Mosin-Nagant, the mighty M1 Garand that gave the American GI a superpower, all the way to the Sturmgewehr 44 — the first assault rifle and arguably the most important gun of the entire 20th century.

videos.title: The Deadliest Battleship of WW2, RANKED by FIREPOWER
videos.description:
Everyone thinks the Bismarck was the deadliest battleship of WW2 — but ranked by pure firepower, it doesn't even crack the top 10.

In this video we rank the 10 deadliest battleships of World War 2 by the one number that actually matters: the raw weight of a single broadside. From a treaty-crippled British giant to a Japanese monster that hurled over 14 TONS of steel in one salvo, we count down every heavyweight — and reveal why the deadliest guns ever built were already obsolete the day they set sail.

We break down the real firepower, combat records, and tragic fates of the King George V, Littorio, Fusō, Colorado, Nagato, the American Standards, Nelson & Rodney, North Carolina & South Dakota, the mighty Iowa — and the undisputed king, Yamato.

Which battleship do YOU think deserved the #1 spot? Drop it in the comments below.

videos.title: Every WW2 Cartridge Explained — Nation by Nation
videos.description:
In 1943, with their cities burning, German engineers built a stubby little rifle round barely longer than your thumb — and accidentally invented the ancestor of the AK-47, the M16, and nearly every assault rifle on Earth today. But that was just one bullet. World War 2 wasn't only fought with tanks and bombers — it was fought with ammunition, dozens of rival cartridges, some deadly, some laughably weak, and some still killing people 80 years later.

This is the story of every major WW2 cartridge, nation by nation — the round that got a US president killed, the Japanese bullet you couldn't see coming, the British rifle so fast the Germans swore they were facing machine guns, and the Soviet cartridge that's still in frontline use more than 130 years after it was born.

Chapters
00:00 The bullet that invented the modern rifle
00:41 Italy
02:36 Japan
04:27 Britain
06:42 The Soviet Union
08:48 The United States
10:58 Germany

Figures based on published military-history and firearms sources. This is educational military history — the story of what these cartridges did and why they mattered, not a how-to.

videos.title: Every Type of WW2 Artillery Explained
videos.description:
World War II artillery was more than just giant cannons. From small infantry mortars to massive railway guns and battleship naval guns, artillery shaped the battlefield in ways tanks and aircraft alone never could.

In this video, we explain every major type of artillery used in World War II, including mortars, mountain and pack guns, anti-tank guns, field howitzers, anti-aircraft guns, self-propelled artillery, assault guns, tank destroyers, rocket artillery, railway guns, and naval guns. Each weapon had a different role: some supported infantry at close range, some destroyed tanks with high-velocity shells, some defended the skies, and others delivered overwhelming firepower from miles away.

You’ll learn how WWII artillery worked, why certain guns became legendary, and how these weapons changed modern warfare forever. From the German 88mm Flak gun and Soviet Katyusha rockets to the American 105mm howitzer, M7 Priest, Schwerer Gustav, and Iowa-class naval guns, this is the complete story of artillery power in World War II.

videos.title: Every Major Pacific Battle of WW2 RANKED by IMPACT
videos.description:
From the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor to the bloody "Typhoon of Steel" at Okinawa, the Pacific Theater of World War 2 produced some of the most decisive, brutal, and history-changing battles ever fought. But which one truly mattered most?

In this video, we rank every major Pacific battle of WW2 by its real impact on the war — the clashes that stopped the Japanese Empire, turned the tide, and set the stage for the final surrender. We break down the strategy, the staggering numbers, and the untold stories behind each turning point.

Discover how U.S. codebreakers set up the ambush at Midway that sank four Japanese carriers in just five minutes… why Guadalcanal became known as the "Island of Death"… how the Battle of Leyte Gulf became the largest naval battle in history… and why the horror of Okinawa helped decide the use of the atomic bomb.

Whether you're a WW2 history buff or new to the Pacific War, this is your complete guide to the battles that decided the fate of the world.

videos.title: How Every WW2 Tank Shell Actually Worked
videos.description:
Two shells hit the same armor plate. One shatters and skips into the trees. The other punches clean through. Same steel, same distance, same caliber — so what's the difference?

The truth is a WW2 tank shell was never one weapon. It was a dozen different weapons wearing the same brass jacket, each built to solve a problem the last one couldn't beat. In this video we break down every major tank round of World War 2 — from the simple solid slug to the tungsten-cored super-penetrators and the chemistry-driven jets that let a single foot soldier kill a 50-ton tank.

We cover how each one worked, why it was invented, and the fatal weakness that forced engineers to build the next one:

CHAPTERS:
00:00 The shell that shouldn't work
High Explosive (HE)
Armor Piercing (AP)
Armor Piercing Capped (APC)
Armor Piercing Ballistic Capped (APBC)
Armor Piercing Capped Ballistic Capped (APCBC)
Armor Piercing High Explosive (APHE)
Armor Piercing Composite Rigid (APCR / HVAP / Pzgr 40)
Armor Piercing Discarding Sabot (APDS)
High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT)
White Phosphorus (WP)

It was a 6-year duel — armor thickening, shells evolving to beat it, armor thickening again. Cap it. Streamline it. Pack it with tungsten. Throw the body away. Swap steel for chemistry. This is the full story of the argument between metal and motion.

If you love military history and how weapons actually work, subscribe for more.
